title: The Fabrication and Operation of a Continuous Flow, Micro-Electroporation System with Permeabilization Detection
protocol: Install a CAD software of choice, design a 2-Dimensional 'mask' of both the microfluidic channel and electrodes, and save the design in desired file format (i.e., .dxf, .dwg).
Send the designed mask to a supplier for printing.
Ensure the dimensions of the designs are within the resolution capabilities of the supplier.
Submerge substrates in an acetone bath for 10 min at room temperature.
Transfer substrates from the acetone bath to an isopropanol (IPA) bath and submerge for 10 min at room temperature.
Move substrates from the IPA bath into a deionized water bath and submerge for 10 min at room temperature.
Remove substrates from the deionized water bath and dry using a pressurized nitrogen or filtered air gas source.
Place dried substrates in a 150 °C oven for a minimum of 30 min to allow evaporation of remaining moisture.
Allow silicon wafer to cool to room temperature after removal from the oven.
Secure silicon wafer to the chuck of the wafer spin coater using the vacuum system.
Program the spinner with Step 1 - 500 rpm for 10 s at an acceleration of 100 rpm/s, and Step 2 - 1000 rpm for 30 s at an acceleration of 300 rpm/s.
Dispense 4 mL of SU-8 2010 photoresist onto the center of the silicon wafer.
Run the programmed spinner sequence.
Turn off the vacuum once the system comes to a halt.
Transfer the SU-8 coated silicon wafer onto a hot plate at 95 °C for 4-5 min for soft bake.
Remove the wafer from the hot plate and allow it to cool to room temperature.
Secure the photomask with the 2D microfluidic channel designs onto the mask holder.
Insert the silicon wafer, with the SU-8 coating facing upwards, onto the wafer chuck.
Set the exposure settings for 150 mJ/cm² and run the machine.
Place the SU-8 coated silicon wafer on a hot plate at 95 °C for 4-5 min for post-exposure bake.
Submerge the silicon wafer in the SU-8 developer solution for 3-4 min, applying gentle agitation.
Remove the wafer from the solution and rinse the surface with IPA.
Dry the surface using a pressurized nitrogen or filtered air gas source.
Inspect the features under a microscope using a UV filter to ensure no obvious defects in the microfluidic channels.
Place the silicon wafer into a 150 °C oven for at least 30 min for hard bake.
Allow the wafer to cool down to room temperature and use stylus profilometry to measure the exact height and slope of the channel sidewalls.
Secure the glass slide to the chuck of the spinner using vacuum.
Program the spinner for Step 1 - 500 rpm for 10 seconds at an acceleration of 100 rpm/s.
Program the spinner for Step 2 - 3000 rpm for 30 seconds at an acceleration of 300 rpm/s.
Dispense 3-4 droplets of HMDS across the surface of the glass slide.
Run the program.
Dispense 1 mL of photoresist onto the surface of the glass slide to cover the surface area.
Run the program.
Turn off the vacuum and remove the glass slide from the spinner once it has stopped.
Place the S1818 coated glass slide on a hot plate at 120 °C for 4 minutes for a soft bake.
Remove the glass slide and allow it to cool to room temperature.
Secure the photomask with the 2D electrode designs onto the mask holder.
Insert and align the glass slide, with the S1818 coating facing upwards, onto the wafer chuck.
Set the exposure settings for 250 mJ/cm² and run the machine.
Submerge the glass slide in MF-319 developer solution for 2 minutes.
Apply gentle agitation to the submerged glass slide.
Rinse the surface of the glass slide with deionized water.
Dry the surface using a pressurized nitrogen or filtered air gas source.
Observe the features under a microscope using a UV filter.
Submerge the glass slide in 10:1 buffered HF solution for 1 min in a polytetrafluoroethylene container.
Transfer and wash the glass slides in deionized water.
Repeat the wash step 3 times.
Dry the surface using a pressurized nitrogen or filtered air gas source.
Place glass substrates in a 65°C oven overnight to remove any remaining moisture.
Cover the substrates from light.
Follow the cleanroom-specific protocol to operate the in-house PVD system.
Sputter titanium for 8 min at a rate of ~100 Å/min.
Sputter platinum for 10 min at a rate of ~200 Å/min.
Remove the substrates from the PVD chamber.
Submerge the metal-coated glass slides in an acetone bath for ~10 min.
Sonicate the bath to introduce agitation to break up the unadhered metal film.
Use an acetone-soaked wipe to remove any residues if necessary.
Wash the electrode patterns with deionized water.
Place the cleaned electrodes in a 65°C oven overnight to remove any remaining surface moisture.
Use stylus profilometry to measure the profile of the patterned electrodes.
Secure the wafer to the bottom of a Petri dish and place the Petri dish into a desiccator.
Surround the perimeter of the silicon wafer with approximately 50 µL of Trichloro(1H,1H,2H,2H-perfluorooctyl) silane.
Connect vacuum and run for 20 min.
Mix PDMS elastomer base to hardener at a 10:1 weight ratio on top of an electronic balance.
Pour the PDMS solution over the silicon wafer and place the mixture under a vacuum to remove all air bubbles.
Cure at 65 °C for a minimum of 4 h allowing the PDMS to solidify.
Cut out the molded PDMS using the tip of a razor blade.
Peel the PDMS from the silicon wafer.
Remove PDMS from the inlet/outlets of the device using a sharpened biopsy punch.
Submerge PDMS devices in IPA and place them into a sonicator for 30-45 min.
Rinse PDMS devices with deionized water.
Place PDMS devices in a 65 °C oven overnight.
Cut the PDMS devices to size.
Ensure the surface of the PDMS device is clean.
Program the plasma generator.
Set Power to 70 W, Time to 35 s, Pressure to 325 mTorr, and Flow Rate of oxygen gas to 60 SCCM.
Place PDMS and electrode glass slide into the system with features facing up.
Run the program.
Remove devices using appropriate tools.
Align channel features to electrodes under a stereoscope.
Apply pressure from the center of PDMS towards the sides to remove air bubbles.
Place the device on a hot plate at 95 °C for at least 2 minutes.
Let the device cool down at room temperature.
Cut two pieces of 22-G solid wire, each approximately 6 inches long.
Strip the insulator from both ends of the wires.
Bond the wires to electrode pads using silver conductive epoxy.
Place completed devices in a 65 °C oven overnight.
Culture HEK293 cells in complete DMEM solution (88% DMEM, 10% heat-inactivated fetal bovine serum, 1% L-glutamine, 1% penicillin-streptomycin) in a T25 flask in an incubator at 37 °C, 95% O2, 5% CO2.
Passage cells when reaching ~80% confluency.
Aspirate the media from the flask using either a pipette or vacuum system.
Incubate the cells in 0.25% trypsin-EDTA (2 mL-T25 flask) for 2 min at 37 °C.
Neutralize trypsin with twice the volume of culture media.
Transfer the cell suspension into a 15 mL conical tube and centrifuge HEK293 cells at 770 x g for 2 min.
Aspirate the supernatant using either a pipette or vacuum system.
Resuspend HEK293 cells in 1 mL of pre-warmed DMEM.
Plate the cells following steps 8.1.7-8.1.8.
Plate the cells at a 10:1 to 20:1 dilution in a T25 flask (5 mL of DMEM) to continue the culture.
Plate the cells at a 5:1 to 20:1 dilution in a 6-well plate (2 mL of DMEM per well) to be harvested for electroporation experiments.
Prepare electroporation buffer.
Wash the cells in sterile 1x PBS.
Transfer cell suspension into a 15 mL conical tube.
Centrifuge cells at 770 x g for 2 min.
Wash HEK293 cell pellet in electroporation buffer.
Centrifuge cells at 770 x g for 2 min.
Resuspend the cells in electroporation buffer at ~5 million cells/mL.
Add pDNA encoding for green fluorescent protein (GFP) to a final concentration of 20 µg/mL.
Gently mix the pDNA/cell suspension and transfer the suspension into a 1 cc syringe for experimentation.
Turn on electronics 20-30 min prior to experiments to warm up.
Set Power Supply 1 to -15 V to power the negative end of the circuit.
Set Power Supply 2 (Function Generator) to output DC signal and set amplitude to 2 V, connecting it to a 50x amplifier input.
Program Electroporation Pulse Generator for square wave pulse width and amplitude as desired.
Set output mode to trigger mode (1 pulse).
Connect the output of the pulse generator to the input of the 50x amplifier.
Set the function generator output to 600 mV for an electric field strength of 1 kV/cm (30 V/50x gain).
Verify outputs of the 50x Amplifier using an oscilloscope.
Output 1-100 V from Power Supply 2.
Connect a 10x probe to an oscilloscope channel and to the micro-device for monitoring electroporation pulse application.
Monitor the system during experimentation to ensure pulses are being applied.
Ensure lock-in USB is connected and registered.
Double-check all lock-in settings in the algorithm code, particularly the lock-in output frequency.
Place the micro-device onto the stage of the microscope via a slide holder.
Turn on the CCD camera and bring the microfluidic channel into focus using a 4x or 10x objective.
Remove all air bubbles from the cell-loaded syringe.
Attach a 30 G needle to the cell-loaded syringe.
Slide tygon tubing down the length of the needle using tweezers.
Pre-fill the outlet reservoir with recovery media, ~40-50 μL.
Apply gentle pressure to the plunger such that fluid slowly reaches the end of the tubing line.
Secure the syringe to the syringe pump.
Turn the syringe pump on and ensure it is set to forward perfusion.
Program the pump for the proper diameter of the syringe.
Set syringe pump flow rate to ~10-20 µL/min.
Allow the pump to run until fluid reaches the end of the tubing line.
Secure tubing to the microfluidic device.
Lower the syringe pump flow rate to ~5-10 µL/min.
Allow the pump to run until all air is expelled from the microfluidic device and cells are traversing to the outlet.
Remove the cells from the outlet via pipette aspiration.
Re-fill the outlet reservoir with recovery media, ~40-50 µL.
Set the syringe pump flow rate to ~0.1-0.3 µL/min for single cell flow through electrodes.
Ensure the system is saving electrical data.
Ensure the system is reliably detecting cells to trigger computer-controlled pulse applications.
Adjust Detection Threshold accordingly.
Set the pulse parameters for the initial, lowest electrical energy electroporation pulse.
Turn on the Output channel for the electroporation pulse generator.
Follow a pre-determined number of cell detection/pulse applications (n = 100).
At the end of each tested condition, aspirate cells from the microdevice outlet and replenish the outlet with recovery media.
Iterate to the next electroporation pulse condition.
Repeat until all electroporation pulse conditions are tested.
Determine the degree of cell membrane permeabilization for each pulse application tested.
Generate the cell membrane permeabilization map.
Determine the electroporation pulse parameters for high-throughput, population-based feedback.
Turn off the syringe pump.
Remove cells from the outlet reservoir.
Replenish the outlet with recovery media.
Set the syringe pump flow rate to ~1-3 µL/min to ensure a flow of single cells through the electrode set.
Ensure the cell transit time between electrodes is ~25 ms.
Set the pulse amplitude to the optimized condition.
Turn off trigger mode.
Set the pulse width to match the cell transit time.
Set the duty cycle such that pulse ON time matches the optimized condition.
Set the Output channel function generator to ON.
Turn on the syringe pump and allow the system to run until the desired number of cells have been electroporated.
Turn off both the syringe pump and the function generator when done.
Transfer the cells from the outlet reservoir into a cell culture flask/plate filled with pre-warmed recovery media.
Place the culture flask/plate in the incubator.
Remove electroporated cells from the incubator after a 24-h incubation period.
Dilute DRAQ5 at a ratio of 1:1000 to achieve a final concentration of 5 µM in the cell culture vessel.
Gently mix the cells with the staining solution.
Incubate the mixture at 37 °C for 5-30 min.
Turn on an epifluorescent microscope, lamp, and cameras.
Bring the cells into focus on the microscope.
Capture a phase-contrast image of the selected field.
Capture epifluorescent images using FITC (GFP) filter.
Capture additional epifluorescent images using Far-Red (DRAQ5) filter.
Analyze the captured image sets manually or via an algorithm.
Count the total number of GFP-positive cells in all the images.
Count the total number of DRAQ5 stained cells in all the images.
Calculate the electroporation transfection efficiency (eTE), which is the ratio of GFP positive cells to DRAQ5 stained cells.
